guarantees.claim: err_processed is high exactly when both reg2hw.cmd.err_processed.q and reg2hw.cmd.err_processed.qe are high.
reg_kmac_en equals the shadowed register field kmac_en.q.
reg_sha3_mode is a type-cast copy of the shadowed register field mode.q, interpreted as sha3_mode_e.
reg_keccak_strength is a type-cast copy of the shadowed register field kstrength.q, interpreted as keccak_strength_e.
event_absorbed is high if and only if app_absorbed satisfies the mubi4 true strict encoding (mubi4_test_true_strict).

The prim_intr_hw instance connects .intr_o to intr_kmac_done_o, .hw2reg_intr_state_de_o to hw2reg.intr_state.kmac_done.de, and .hw2reg_intr_state_d_o to hw2reg.intr_state.kmac_done.d; its event input is event_absorbed, and control/status signals come from reg2hw fields.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.cmd.err_processed.qe is a one-cycle strobe, ensuring err_processed is a one-cycle pulse when asserted.
assumptions.cond: when err_processed is intended to be used as a single-cycle event
assumptions.risk: If qe remains high for multiple cycles, err_processed stays high, potentially triggering multiple done events or violating downstream handshake expectations.

assumptions.claim: sha3_absorbed must be a one-cycle pulse when its mubi4 true strict condition arises; it must not remain in the true strict state continuously.
assumptions.risk: If sha3_absorbed stays true longer than a cycle, the assertion fails and downstream logic relying on a pulse may behave incorrectly (e.g., double processing).

assumptions.claim: app_absorbed is always a legal mubi4 encoding (true or false), so mubi4_test_true_strict produces a clean logic value without X.
assumptions.risk: If app_absorbed takes an illegal or metastable value, event_absorbed may become X, potentially causing unknown behavior in the interrupt controller (intr_kmac_done_o) or logic that reads it.

uncertain_points.claim: reg_sha3_mode and reg_keccak_strength are created by raw type casts from cfg_shadowed fields without detecting illegal values. An illegal write to those fields could drive invalid enum states into the SHA-3 datapath.
uncertain_points.cond: when software writes an out-of-bounds value to cfg_shadowed.mode or cfg_shadowed.kstrength
uncertain_points.risk: Invalid SHA-3 mode or strength could result in incorrect cryptographic operations, silent data corruption, or security bypass.

uncertain_points.claim: err_processed is expected to be a one-cycle pulse as asserted, but the downstream consumer (not shown in this chunk) must latch or process it correctly. Without understanding that latch, the assertion alone doesn't confirm functional correctness.
uncertain_points.risk: If downstream logic expects level-sensitive handling or multiple cycles, the design may miss events or count them twice.

uncertain_points.claim: sha3_absorbed's pulse requirement is checked by an assertion, but the consuming logic (likely inside sha3) is not visible. If the consumer uses a level or needs stable assertion, a single-cycle pulse could be missed.
uncertain_points.risk: Missed or duplicate absorb events, breaking the absorb protocol.

uncertain_points.claim: event_absorbed is a combinational output of app_absorbed via mubi4_test_true_strict. If app_absorbed is not registered and can glitch, transient false events could appear on event_absorbed and trigger spurious interrupts.
uncertain_points.cond: when app_absorbed changes state asynchronously or has timing glitches
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious interrupts may mislead software, waste CPU time, or, in a secure context, serve as a side channel or denial-of-service vector if the interrupt path is not hardened.
